en: Making them serve the hero,
Driving grief from the people,
The finest came to the horde,
Leaving the horde, he rallied the people,
He would tell everything to the people,
From the hands of the wearied province,
He would leave them unharmed,
His life endured four days of trial,
The people’s vast lineage,
The entrusted tribute,
Gathering all the people,
The legacy mounted by the pasha,
Ask nothing of the inheritance,
The heirloom’s thoroughbred,
For this entire host was stern,
For this whole multitude was wondrous,
The mounted people were renowned,
The heroes ran and assembled,
All day long they met,
The gathered people recited at home,
Cloudlike, they surged in alarm,
The children of the people made ready,
Preparing to fight the unruly host,
All the people ran together,
Those of sound mind did not stay behind,
Those ignorant from of old,
Wondering how many people would go,
The people grieved and stood immense,
Young boys ran about,
The champions who staked their lives,
Were chosen for the mass contest,
Mounting up and drawing level,
The people cried out and the nation stirred,
The khan’s camp thundered,
Kabay cast on his great coat,
His rounded garment bulging,
Ask not of his lament,
Aykanysh in the lofty tower,
Her two thousand put on their gear,
Saying the road had opened,
Restless souls appeared,
When she sent the wretched one into sorrow,
The course of the road became known,
Donning many a gold robe,
His falconlike form appeared,
Straining like a blue-gray stallion,
Those they loved were content at heart,
When found, he understood,
A hero mounted upon three steeds,
His remaining keen sword,
The watching people stirred,
From the world where his life lay,
His ambition began to rise,
What this courageous one knew,
The courageous need a people,
And the good men, without exception,
A courage-less gossip,
When a holy campaign begins,
When an uproar rises among your people,
With your foremost elder as the banner,
If he appears a hero from youth,
If he encircles all who act,
Submitting to a single treasury,
Souls apart [?],
The dark ravine, the dense [?],
The dark one thirsting to drink blood,
Champions who gathered their weapons,
Without talking much or uttering words,
The people's worthy man is a pure man.
All the people submitted,
If there is an enemy, his true companion,
Putting on battle dress,
There is a champion, one or two,
From the wretch who listened to gossip,
Is there a single word from his offspring?
When the people stir, without making war,
A man whose courage is lofty,
Courage, poor wretch, the people's support,
Without making his body wolf-like with a sword,
All valor becoming practiced,
The whole world becomes accustomed,
Would the mind not be overwhelmed?
A commander of troops, a leader of men,
An equal man who speaks fully,
The mist seen upon the mountain,
When the enemy is alarmed, toward the piebald,
Thinking much of the forest switches,
If this experienced man speaks softly.
By becoming a hero and prospering,
The farsighted one who ruled the people,
The grave-eyed legacy,
The weight of the ancestral homeland,
What he did anew,
Since you became the dark city,
What he called the people—this is true.
Taking power into his hands,
The justice that was set in motion,
Setting it upon his own path,
Whenever turmoil rose, the people grew still,
Charcoal-burner, what is your sorrow?
Your soul is at an unreachable distance,
Does your spirit spread out like spring?
Is it a gray waste no living soul has trodden?
Blood would freeze when the soul departed,
If the heart closes, is there an enemy?
Is there another honest mountain?
Is there an enemy among those who would fight us?
Speak of the thought-filled corsac in your sheath,
What do you know—is it needed,
Tell the truth that is in your heart.
Oh, since morning this place has held me,
My eyes are tearful and clouded,
Here is the boundless people without you,
Ride against the enemy, shed blood,
Here is the man who will be your companion.
When the forest's breast surges,
Here is the soaring, boundless lake,
Longing toward the four directions [?],
Here is the man who has fought,
Alas, while strength still remains in you,
Where are your people, burdened by my suffering?
After saying, “like an enemy,”
After Bolot heard the words,
He settled himself with a swagger,
Girding on the Kyngyz sword,
Like a cloud about to rain again,
Wrath spread across his face,
His thoughts turned to Esen,
His heroic bearing became visible,
The wretched soul who stood alone,
Flared up and sprang apart,
Growing desperate, his venom was strong,
Of the gleaming poor fellow,
Today his heroic bearing appeared,
He had one grievance against Esen,
Hearing that the enemy had come,
If he cried out, it was to thrust a spear,
If he desired it, it was to seize Bolot,
His one stratagem was complete, his venom strong,
Hearing that the enemy had come,
How could I ever surrender him?
Hearing that he would make him a mullah,
If a champion hero is born of a girl,
His intent turns sly,
I struck, saying he would destroy him,
Grieving as though chilled through,
Roaming about, burning with grief,
Many souls are brought into being,
There is but one God who creates,
If he makes anyone weak,
What would happen if he chose not to create?
The coarse Könök, the enemy, was broken,
I struck, saying, “Come mowing them down,”
The broad-chested one whose purpose reached its mark,
I struck, saying he would drive them here,
Pouring blood into the dark water,
I struck, crying, “Morning Star!”
When he grew furious, he swaggered,
I struck, saying he would take a life,
Bolot, hear your khan from the chamber,
My people, hear your khan from the prison,
As for me, without lying idle or failing to take it,
How could I hand over the elder?
This seems to be at your root, crafty Kenesh,
Let me test myself against him once,
Let me offer my abundant greeting,
From the venom of the powerful fist,
Now show a little of what you can do,
Let me see your prowess,
Zhalkaitak spoke his words of resolve,
Let me take a chance!
After he had spoken thus,
Esen rose and stepped apart,
His heroic aspect became visible,
Blood drained from the khan’s outward appearance,
The strength left his gaze,
His life departed from his heart,
His spirit surged forth with courage,
His heroic appearance became visible,
A vigilant soul, master of the gauntlet,
Alighting, he moved off afterward,
Utterly composed, his heart was unfeeling,
It became clear what kind of soul he was,
His distant ancestor was Kökbörü,
The lone gray-maned hero,
Hearing of that one’s wrath,
It became clear that he was his descendant,
A champion whose deeds of valor were proclaimed,
It became clear what kind of soul he was,
A life-companion at his side,
Being a fortress for his people,
To the lord descended from a hero.
His eyes blazed like a lion
The people stirred from every side
Many arrived, driving a thousand
He made all the warriors advance
His valor rose in rivalry
I made it a wonder for the ages
The fortress of three hundred heroes
He resolved that he himself would go
All the heroes were roused
They remained whispering
Shotkay threw them all into tumult
I entered beneath the standard
We saw lands known to men
They caught sight of the enemy
My people began to speak
Starting a quarrel unknown to the people
The whole camp fell silent
Neither wisdom nor the people knew
Unable to speak, he fell silent
The messenger who knew the reason
A contentious soul who knew no reason
Making his name and fame known
He guarded it with his courage
Making them all equal before his people
Calling him a youth who struck one by one
What became of our people
Calling him the commoner who saw the marvel
Whispering, turning it into a stream
Remain apart from the clamor of strife
Without paying the levy of the host
At the place where the palace stood
Among a thousand unknown souls
We went about amid the people’s clamor
The place where the people stood in uproar
He reached it and took the reins
Hero Kenen besieged them
Calling it the inheritance named by my khan father
If he is a hero and a champion
If he is a man who takes after his ancestor
If he is an equal defender of the people
We shall keep and train the swift horse
If he is a khan who takes after his father
If he is a soul of noble lineage
Rich in courage though wisdom falls short
Making Ala Köödön a lord
If he is an unworthy fierce warrior
We shall choose a young brave man
If he is a hero equal to any
We shall wait and rule the people
A settled camp, a sheltered place
We shall find the inside of a reserve
The writing left by someone
You came before us face to face
Quarreling as though bound together
When he struck once, he drew it away
One house was given in the khan’s time
We shall break the enclosure
Fighting with turbans drawn tight
Will my twisted fate be set straight
If one man speaks, let him be support
We shall test one hero in victory
Thus was what I said
These were the people he spoke of
I am the man who emerged after being struck
